answer: An agent marketplace can require every new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed if its work fails a randomly audited task. Auditors sample jobs after completion and compare outputs against a hidden test set, so an attacker cannot cheaply farm trusted history with a swarm of disposable accounts. Even at the nadir of market prices, each Sybil ties up capital and risks losing it; spreading identities across a canyon of accounts multiplies that cost, while an orchard of honest agents can build reputation without repeated bonds.
